text:
ashley: Quick heads-up: a staging repro where a paused streaming cursor couldn't resume after its prefix was evicted. Saw 404 from the fast read path.

ashley: TL;DR: prefix eviction removed cached cursor kvs; resume expects them and fails. Durable state was fine but not consulted.

diego: Is this new or related to past tombstone races?

ashley: Related family but distinct: earlier we had stale visibility; here it's a missing-fast-path vs durable fallback gap.

priya: How common are idle cursors in that pool?

ashley: quick staging query: ~1.2k cursors total, ~350 idle >5m, ~80 idle >10m. Eviction threshold set to 10m for that pool.

sam: Options brainstormed: pin-on-open (keep in mem while cursor exists), checkpoint-on-pause to durable, on-resume rehydrate from logs, or keep tiny persistent 'anchor' metadata that survives eviction and triggers async rebuild.

diego: Tradeoffs: pin = steady memory cost; checkpoint = write amp; rehydrate-on-demand = slower resume; anchor = small metadata cost + added eviction class.

ruslan: Anchor idea sketch: write `cursor:anchor:<id>` (very small payload: epoch, durable_ptr) with a TTL 1-3x pause timeout. Eviction releases payload but anchor sits in a meta-slab favored to survive. On resume miss, read anchor -> if found trigger async rehydrate pipeline to restore prefix payload, validate epoch to avoid races.

emma: Need to think correctness on concurrent writes: resume + client append could interleave. If epoch differs, reject rehydrate and read fresh durable state. That implies rehydrate must fetch a durable snapshot and apply idempotent merge.

priya: Monitoring: add rehydrate_attempts, rehydrate_success, rehydrate_latency_hist, rehydrate_cause (evict|missing_durable). Alert if >1% resumes require full log replay or if median rehydrate >500ms.

sam: SLA considerations: hosted customers expect snappy resume. Async rehydrate may add 50-300ms tail. We can tier: default anchor+async for hosted, opt-in pin-on-open for Dedicated/enterprise.

diego: Implementation concerns: reserve small meta-slab for anchors. Estimations: 64B per anchor -> 10k anchors = 640KB. But multi-tenant worst-case could be larger; need caps and overflow eviction policy (e.g., drop oldest anchors and treat subsequent resumes as full-rehydrate).

ashley: UX behavior for clients: on resume miss + anchor present -> return resume-pending (202) with short-poll backoff or server push if connection supports. If no anchor -> immediate fallback to durable read or fail.

ruslan: Rehydrate pipeline details: schedule background worker limited by tenant rate; coalesce duplicate rehydrates for same prefix; idempotent apply using epoch check; mark telemetry when rehydrate completes. Rate-limit and backoff to prevent thundering herd during churn.

emma: Also add tracing spans across eviction->resume->rehydrate to correlate user tickets. We'll need context IDs in anchor metadata.

priya: Testing plan: synthetic harness to create N cursors, idle them, force eviction, then issue concurrent resumes with different arrival patterns. Chaos tests: evict during resume, also simulate durable writes during rehydrate to validate epoch checks.

sam: Rollout plan: prototype on staging pool A; measure rehydrate latency and % resumed from cache vs async. If <1% bad resumes and <200ms median rehydrate, gamma rollout to hosted. Add config flags to enable pin-on-open for Dedicated.

diego: I'll take the prototype (anchor + rehydrate worker). ashley will own RFC + test harness. emma will add metrics + traces. priya + sam will run load/chaos. ruslan to assist on eviction class meta-slab sizing.

oncall-bot: created playbook pointer -> /playbooks/cursor-resume (auto).

ashley: Action items:
- diego: PoC anchor + async rehydrate (2w spike)
- emma: metrics + tracing + alert (parallel)
- priya + sam: load/chaos tests (parallel)
- ruslan: meta-slab sizing & overflow policy proposal
- ashley: RFC + rollout checklist + client UX contract (today)

sam: Add note: make rehydrate idempotent and coalescing to avoid worker thrash.

diego: noted. Will include dedupe + rate-limit in PoC.

ashley: I'll link RFC/PR back to this thread when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

emma: One more ops note: surface per-tenant rehydrate error counts in Console, so SEs can diagnose big tenants.

ashley: Agreed. Put that in telemetry doc. Will update RFC.
